summary: David Shulman is an Indologist who studied at Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1967–1971) and the University of London (~1972–1976). He held long-term appointments at Hebrew University of Jerusalem, including as Professor of Indian Studies and Comparative Religion (~1976–1995).

David Tracy is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Saint Joseph's Seminary and the Pontifical Gregorian University. He taught at the Catholic University of America (~1965–1969), the University of Chicago (~1969–2006), and the Committee on Social Thought (~1987–2006).

David W. Chappell was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology who completed doctoral work at Yale University (~1968–1976). He served as a professor at the University of Hawaii (~1972–2000) and held a post at Soka University of America (~2000–2004).

David W. Tien is a scholar of sinology and philosophy. He studied at McGill University, the University of Toronto, and the University of Michigan (attested 2009, PhD), where he was supervised by James Robson and also studied under Robert H. Sharf.
David Webster is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Bristol, studying under doctoral supervisor Peter Harvey.

Dawa Norbu was a Tibetologist and historian who studied at the University of Delhi (~1970–1974) and UC Berkeley (~1976–1982). He held posts at San Francisco State University, University of San Francisco, CIIS, and Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1983–2006).

Daya Ram Sahni was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Oriental College, Lahore (~1898–1903). He served with the Archaeological Survey of India as Deputy for Exploration (1931–1935) and was Jaipur State's Director of Archæology and Historical Research in 1935.

Dayong was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied at Wuchang Buddhist Institute and under Palden Tenzin Nyendrak, Taixu, and Bai Puren. He taught at Wuchang Buddhist Institute in 1923 and founded the Tibetan Language School of Beijing.
Debala Mitra was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied under Dineschandra Sircar. She served as Director at the Archaeological Survey of India from around 1952 to 1983.
Debi Prasanna Pattanayak is an Indian linguist and Indologist who studied at Cornell University (~1959–1961). He served as director of the Central Institute of Indian Languages in 1988.

Debiprasad Chattopadhyaya was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Calcutta (~1935–1942) under Surendranath Dasgupta. He later held an academic post at the University of Calcutta from roughly 1956 to 1980.
Deborah Carlson is an archaeologist. Her career includes attested affiliations in 2015 with Texas A&M University and the Institute of Nautical Archaeology.

Deborah Klimburg-Salter is an art historian and Tibetologist who studied at the University of Vienna and Harvard University (~1969–1976) under Oleg Grabar. She served as a professor at the University of Vienna, where she held posts from ~1990 into the 2010s.
Declan Quigley is an Indologist who has held teaching posts at the University of Cambridge, the University of St Andrews, and Queen's University Belfast.

Dedong Wei is a scholar of religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Renmin University of China (~1995–1998), where he became an associate professor of religious studies around 2002.

Denis Twitchett was a sinologist and historian educated at SOAS (~1942–1943) and St Catharine's College (~1946–1950). He held professorships at the University of London (~1960–1968) and Cambridge (attested 1973–1986), and was emeritus at Princeton University (~1980–1994).

Denma Lochö Rinpoche was a figure in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology who studied at Drepung Loseling Monastery (~1940–1953). He served as a Visiting Scholar at the University of Virginia around 1978.

Dennis A. Johnson is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Vienna, earning his Magister der Philosophie under MA supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2012).

Dennis Hirota is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at UC Berkeley and Nagoya University. He served as a professor at Ryukoku University (~1995) and held a post at the Hongwanji International Center (attested 1998).

Derek F. Maher is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned degrees from Evergreen State College and the University of Virginia, studying under Jeffrey Hopkins. He lectured at Virginia and UNC Greensboro, and co-directed Religious Studies at East Carolina University.
